recommendation.recommendation: Implement immediate targeted irrigation to relieve severe water stress in the cotton field.
recommendation.justification: Satellite NDVI shows excellent canopy health (0.75) but NDWI indicates high water stress (-0.35) and weather data reports no recent precipitation. Soil health is optimal (score 92, pH 6.25, medium nitrogen and organic carbon) and ambient temperature/humidity are within cotton's ideal range. Immediate irrigation will protect yield potential, prevent drought‑related diseases (e.g., Fusarium wilt), and capitalize on the strong vegetative growth already present.
actions: Apply flood irrigation today to raise soil moisture to field capacity (~0.32 m³/m³). Target 30‑35 mm of water per application, adjusting for the 32 % clay content to avoid waterlogging.
Establish an irrigation schedule of every 7‑10 days, monitoring soil moisture sensors to keep volumetric water content between wilting point (0.14) and field capacity.
Lay a 5‑10 cm layer of organic mulch (straw or shredded leaves) after irrigation to reduce evaporation and soil exposure.
Inspect drainage pathways and create shallow furrows if necessary to prevent surface runoff on the clayey sections of the field.
Record irrigation volume, timing, and any observed runoff in a field log for future adjustments.
recommendation.expected_outcome: Restored soil moisture will eliminate critical water stress, sustain the high canopy vigor, and maintain expected cotton yield and fiber quality, while minimizing risk of drought‑induced diseases and soil erosion.
monitoring_plan: Daily visual check of plant turgidity and leaf wilting.
Measure soil moisture at 20 cm depth with a handheld probe after each irrigation event.
Weekly review of NDWI from satellite imagery (target >0.10) to confirm reduced water stress.
Bi‑weekly scouting for Fusarium wilt or other stress‑related disease symptoms.
Track market price trends and plan harvest logistics once boll formation begins.
